episode: Sesoösis's campaign to conquer the inhabited world (Ethiopia; Red Sea coasts to India; Asia to the Tanais; Thrace)
passages: Diod. 1.54.4 (army levied: foot, horse, war chariots); 1.54.5 (count of the companion-commanders); 1.55.2 (fleet sent into the Red Sea)
purported_date: Undated in the text (seven generations after Moeris); king usually identified with Senusret I/III (c. 1970-1840 BCE) with Ramesside elements (13th c. BCE)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii) (on every candidate date)
evidence: Known only as Greek reports of an Egyptian priestly legend: Herodotus 2.102-110 (c. 430 BCE), Manetho, Diodorus (c. 60-30 BCE, prob. via Hecataeus of Abdera c. 300 BCE), not independent; contemporary Senusret III texts (Semna stelae, Khusobek stela) record limited Nubian/Levantine campaigns, not this world conquest. Hard case: composite king
side2_polity: Peoples conquered on the campaign (no single opponent; uncounted)

text: Diodorus, Library 2.1-20 (Ninus and Semiramis, from Ctesias)
episode: Ninus's war against Bactria (Oxyartes), incl. the siege of Bactra
passages: Diod. 2.5.4 (Assyrian army: foot, horse, scythed chariots, citing Ctesias); 2.6.2 (Bactrian levy under Oxyartes)
purported_date: Late 3rd-early 2nd millennium BCE (Ctesian chronology: Assyrian empire lasting more than 1,300 years before its fall, Diod. 2.21.8); Ninus is a legendary eponym of Nineveh
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Known only from Ctesias, Persica (written c. 390s BCE), as excerpted by Diodorus (c. 60-30 BCE); no Assyrian record or archaeology of such a war; earliest form well over a millennium after the purported date

text: Diodorus, Library 2.1-20 (Ninus and Semiramis, from Ctesias)
episode: Darius I's campaign against the European Scythians [digression: Diodorus's own comparison at 2.5.5, not part of the Ctesian narrative; author to confirm inclusion]
purported_date: c. 513 BCE (Herodotus; modern consensus c. 513/512 BCE)
criterion: A (iii): two independent ancient narratives; (i) arguable via DNa
evidence: Herodotus 4.83-144 (c. 430 BCE) and Ctesias F13 (c. 390s BCE) give accounts differing in detail; Darius's tomb inscription DNa (c. 490 BCE) lists 'Scythians across the sea' among subjects; cf. Frame W W141. If Ctesias is judged derivative of Herodotus, recode M (Herodotus c. 80 yrs after)

text: Diodorus, Library 2.1-20 (Ninus and Semiramis, from Ctesias)
episode: Dionysius I of Syracuse's campaigns (wars with Carthage), forces not tied to one campaign [digression: Diodorus's own comparison at 2.5.6; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: Diod. 2.5.6 (foot and horse led out from Syracuse; warships from a single harbour)
purported_date: 398-367 BCE (Dionysius I's Carthaginian wars; the passage names no single campaign)
criterion: M: episode not fixed to one event, so (i)-(iii) cannot be applied to it
evidence: Dionysius's wars are well attested (Diodorus 13-15 from Philistus/Timaeus; Plato Ep. 8 c. 353 BCE; siege works at Motya, 397 BCE), but 2.5.6 names no campaign; if tied to the 398-397 BCE campaign, A via (ii); cf. Frame W W228, W231

text: Diodorus, Library 2.1-20 (Ninus and Semiramis, from Ctesias)
episode: Roman enrolment of all Italians fit for service against the Gallic invasion of 225 BCE ('a little before Hannibal') [digression: Diodorus's own comparison at 2.5.7; a muster, not a field army; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: Diod. 2.5.7 (all Romans and allies fit for service enrolled)
purported_date: 225 BCE (Polybius 2.23-24; Diodorus gives no date beyond 'a little before Hannibal')
criterion: A (i): written source composed within 50 yrs (Fabius Pictor, a participant)
evidence: Fabius Pictor (wrote c. 210-200 BCE; cited by Eutropius 3.5, Orosius 4.13, Pliny NH 3.138); Polybius 2.22-31 (c. 150 BCE) partly depends on him; identifying Diodorus's war with 225 BCE is standard but inferred; cf. Frame W W415 (Telamon)

text: Diodorus, Library 2.1-20 (Ninus and Semiramis, from Ctesias)
episode: Semiramis's invasion of India (Stabrobates): battle on the Indus and land battle beyond it
passages: Diod. 2.17.1 (Semiramis's army: foot, horse, chariots, citing Ctesias); 2.17.2 (camel-riders; river boats); 2.17.5 (Stabrobates' reed river boats); 2.18.6 (detachment left to guard the pontoon bridge)
sides_counted: Both sides (Indian side: river boats only)
purported_date: As Ninus's widow in the Ctesian chronology (late 3rd-early 2nd millennium BCE); the name's historical model, Sammu-ramat, fl. c. 811-792 BCE
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii) (on either date)
evidence: Known only from Ctesias (c. 390s BCE) via Diodorus (c. 60-30 BCE); no Assyrian record of an Indian campaign; even from the historical Sammu-ramat the gap exceeds 400 yrs; later mentions (Megasthenes, Nearchus in Strabo/Arrian) belong to the same Greek tradition

episode: The Achaean expedition against Troy (Trojan War); the Trojan allies as its other side
passages: Il. 2.494-759 (a ship count closes each Achaean contingent; men per ship stated at 2.509-510 and 2.719-720); the Trojan catalogue 2.816-877 gives no numbers
criterion: M: disputed whether archaeology or contemporary Hittite texts attest this event
evidence: Iliad fixed c. 750-650 BCE (consensus), >=450 yrs after; Greek epic is the only narrative tradition, but whether the Troy VI/VIIa destructions or 13th-c. BCE Hittite texts on Wilusa and Ahhiyawa (Tawagalawa, Manapa-Tarhunta letters) attest this war is disputed; cf. Frame W W045

episode: War between Rome and Alba Longa under Tullus Hostilius, decided by the champions' combat of the Horatii and Curiatii [borderline: the only count is of the champions, not of the armies; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: Livy 1.24.1-2 (champions chosen from each army); 1.25.1-14 (their combat)
purported_date: c. 672-640 BCE (reign of Tullus Hostilius, Varronian chronology)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Known only from the Roman annalistic tradition: Livy 1.22-29 (c. 27-25 BCE) and Dionysius Ant. Rom. 3.2-31 (from 7 BCE), both from the annalists (not independent, Amendment 1.2); earliest annalist Fabius Pictor c. 200 BCE, still >=400 yrs after; no event-specific archaeology

episode: Tullus Hostilius's war with the Sabines (battle at the Silva Malitiosa)
passages: Livy 1.30.3 (squadrons of cavalry enrolled from the Albans; legions filled up and new ones raised); 1.30.4-10 (the war, won by the enlarged cavalry)
purported_date: c. 672-640 BCE (reign of Tullus Hostilius, Varronian chronology; Frame W gives 653 BC)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Livy (c. 27-25 BCE) and Dionysius Ant. Rom. 3 (from 7 BCE) share the annalistic source; earliest annalist Fabius Pictor c. 200 BCE, >=400 yrs after; no contemporary record or event-specific archaeology; cf. Frame W W093 (Battle of Malitiosa Forest)

episode: Tarquinius Priscus's war with the Sabines (battles at the Anio)
passages: Livy 1.36.1-2 and 1.36.7-8 (cavalry centuries brought to a stated total of horsemen); 1.37.1-6 (the renewed battle with the enlarged cavalry)
purported_date: c. 616-579 BCE (reign of Tarquinius Priscus, Varronian chronology)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Livy (c. 27-25 BCE) and Dionysius Ant. Rom. 3.55-66 (from 7 BCE) share the annalistic source; earliest annalist Fabius Pictor c. 200 BCE, >=370 yrs after; no contemporary record or event-specific archaeology

episode: The Cattle Raid of Cooley: the host of Ailill and Medb against Ulster, to the final battle at Gáirech and Irgáirech
passages: O'Rahilly 1976 translation page (edition lines). Connacht-led host: p. 125 (ll. 1-24: forces of the sons of Mágu; Cormac Conn Longas's men and companies); p. 126 (ll. 25-62: Fergus's exiles); p. 128 (ll. 107-138: Medb's chariot escort); pp. 129-130 (ll. 139-209: Medb's retinue, the Maines', Munster kings' and Gailióin divisions; divisions in the camp); p. 134 (ll. 327-355: marginal note counting the divisions); p. 148 (ll. 813-843: Fráech's company); p. 157 (ll. 1137-1176: Lugaid's horsemen at the parley); p. 158 (ll. 1177-1214: Ailill's division joins Fergus's company); p. 168 (ll. 1540-1577: band sent against Cú Chulainn at once); p. 171 (ll. 1645-1678: warriors sent against the boy-troop; men sent with the maid); p. 181 (ll. 2011-2048: attackers sent together); p. 182 (ll. 2049-2082: Medb's household band); p. 194 (ll. 2505-2538: band of Ferchú Loingsech, an exile of Ailill's); p. 195 (ll. 2539-2570: band sent by Medb); p. 236 (ll. 4089-4122: Fergus's division and the divisions of Medb, Ailill and their sons). Ulster: p. 170 (ll. 1612-1644) and pp. 184-185 (ll. 2117-2203: the boy-troop of Emain); p. 171 (ll. 1645-1678: Rochad's men); p. 214 (ll. 3328-3356: companies of Fintan, Mend and Rochad); p. 215 (ll. 3357-3390: Ulster charioteers at Tailtiu); p. 219 (ll. 3498-3533: Conchobar's chariot-fighters; companies awaited); pp. 221-229 (ll. 3569-3877: Mac Roth's count of the Ulster companies; Conchobar's sons' divisions); p. 233 (ll. 3987-4019: chariots of the warriors from Iruath)
purported_date: c. 1st c. BCE-1st c. CE (Irish synthetic history makes Conchobar a contemporary of Christ)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Rec. I compiled from Old Irish material of the 8th c. (Thurneysen; some layers perhaps 7th c.), in Lebor na hUidre c. 1100: >=600 yrs after; no contemporary writing in Ireland; Emain Macha and Crúachain archaeology is not event-specific; Rec. II is the same tradition
side1_polity: Connacht (Ailill and Medb) with the men of Ireland (Leinster incl. the Gailióin, Munster, Ulster exiles)

episode: Raid on Emain Macha by men from the Isles of Faiche during the Ulstermen's debility (Boyhood Deeds flashback) [borderline: a raiding band, not an army; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: O'Rahilly 1976 translation p. 140 (ed. ll. 528-563: the raiders' band, in 'The Boyhood Deeds')
purported_date: Some years before the Táin, c. 1st c. BCE-1st c. CE (same basis as T-OT-011)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Known only from this flashback in Táin Rec. I (8th-c. Old Irish material; Lebor na hUidre c. 1100); no independent evidence
side1_polity: Raiders from the Isles of Faiche (not located by the text)

text: Hervarar saga ok Heiðreks (battle of the Goths and Huns)
episode: War of the Huns (Humli and Hlöðr) against the Goths (Angantýr): attack on Hervör's fortress and the battle on Dúnheiðr
passages: Hervarar saga, Guðni Jónsson & Bjarni Vilhjálmsson ed. (Fornaldar sögur Norðurlanda, 1943-44; heimskringla.no text): ch. XII (prose: the Hunnish levy by battalions and companies); ch. XIII (Gizurr's stanza on the Hunnish host, Hlöðskviða)
purported_date: Contested; the saga gives no date; usually linked to Gothic-Hunnic conflicts of c. 375-450s CE
criterion: M: event date and the tradition's fixation date both too contested to apply the 300-year rule
evidence: Saga written 13th c. (Hauksbók c. 1302-10; R 15th c.); embedded poem older but undated; Old English Widsith (Exeter Book c. 975, composed 7th-10th c.) names the same heroes and a Gothic defence against Attila's people: one Germanic legendary tradition, post-500, so no (iii); if Widsith is 7th c. the gap may be under 300 yrs
side2_polity: Goths (King Angantýr; Árheimar on the Dnieper)

episode: Jimmu's eastern expedition: conquest of the Yamato basin (Kunimi hill, Shiki, Nagasunehiko) [borderline: the counts are a numeral in the epithet takeru 'bravos', generally read as a conventional 'many', plus a count of enemy bands; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: NS 3, year tsuchinoe-uma, 9th month (bravos of Kunimi hill, Shiki and Akagane, with a numeral); 10th month (attack on the Kunimi-hill bravos; remaining enemy bands counted); 11th month (Ye-shiki gathers the bravos); year tsuchinoto-hitsuji, 2nd month (variant: Shiki bravos at Iware)
purported_date: 667-660 BCE (Nihon shoki chronology: expedition from the kinoe-tora year to accession in the kanoto-tori year)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Known only from the court tradition of Nihon shoki (720 CE) and Kojiki (712 CE), which share sources (not independent); >1,300 yrs after the purported date; no inscriptions or event-specific archaeology
side2_polity: Chiefs of the Yamato basin (Nagasunehiko, Ye-shiki, the bravos of Kunimi hill)

episode: Keikō's campaign against the Kumaso in Kyushu [borderline: the Kumaso count is a numeral in the epithet takeru 'bravos'; the other count is a soldier escort; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: NS 7, Keikō year 12, 12th month (the Kumaso 'bravos' epithet with a numeral; soldiers given to Ichifukaya)
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii)
evidence: Nihon shoki (720 CE); Kojiki has only Yamato Takeru's Kumaso exploit; Bungo/Hizen fudoki (c. 730s) repeat the court tradition; >600 yrs after the purported date

episode: Jingū's expedition against Silla [borderline: the only count is the stock Chinese formula for 'the whole army' (a count of armies); Silla's tribute ships excluded; author to confirm inclusion]
passages: NS 9, Chūai year 9, 9th and 10th months (the Empress's orders to the army, in the stock numeral formula)
purported_date: 200 CE (Nihon shoki chronology, Chūai 9); often redated by modern scholars (+120 yrs, or to the Wa campaigns of 391-400 CE)
criterion: M: purported date contested; possible link to a contemporary inscription
evidence: Nihon shoki (720 CE) and Kojiki (712 CE), one tradition; the Gwanggaeto Stele (414 CE) and Samguk sagi record Wa attacks on Silla, and some link this campaign to those of 391-400 CE on the Stele (which would meet (i)); others see no historical basis

episode: Rebellion of Prince Oshikuma (with Kagosaka) against Jingū, ending at Ausaka and the Seta crossing in Ōmi
passages: NS 9, Jingū regency year 1, 3rd month (force led by Takeuchi no Sukune and Takefurukuma, with a numeral; the stock 'armies' formula repeated)
purported_date: 201 CE (Nihon shoki chronology, regency year 1); c. 321 CE on the common +120-year correction
criterion: U: one tradition; earliest form >=300 yrs after; none of (i)-(iii) (on either date)
evidence: Nihon shoki (720 CE) and Kojiki (712 CE), one court tradition; c. 400 yrs after even with the +120-yr correction; no inscriptions or archaeology
